posts.hook: The CEO who built Nvidia may be out by the end of the week
posts.caption: nvidia's board is preparing to oust jensen huang, according to wsj sources, google launched a decision model that scores answers without writing text, and aws released a local emulator it says no engineer wrote or reviewed. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, WSJ sources say
slides.desc: A second affair report, this one inside the company. Shares ==fell more than 9%== after hours.

slides.title: Commerce is closing the rented-chip gap in China export rules
slides.desc: Rules restrict where a chip ships, not who uses it remotely. A new one would cover both.

slides.title: Google ships Gemini Decision 1: a model that scores answers, never writes text
slides.desc: Yes/no, choice and rubric questions in one pass, $0.10 per million input tokens.

slides.title: AWS releases a local emulator and says its team ==never wrote or reviewed the code==
slides.desc: Agents built it. Free, open source, 200+ services on a laptop instead of a deployment.

slides.title: United won't let AI agents book your flight
slides.desc: It cites data exposure, unintended purchases and federal disclosure rules.

slides.title: TSMC will put up to $1B into OpenAI and Anthropic
slides.desc: The chipmaker buys into its customers' customers. Analysts call the money circular.

slides.title: Krebs traces the operator of Qilin to a 36-year-old in St. Petersburg
slides.desc: The group claims at least 365 victims in three months. Reused old handles gave him away.

terms.gloss: the most active ransomware group, renting its tools to other hackers
